confirmed: CFTC Letter 26-05 defines a pre-GENIUS payment stablecoin using issuer status, permitted reserve assets and monthly attestation criteria. It is conditional staff no-action relief, not a rule or token-specific approval.
Circle Internet Financial LLC is listed by NYDFS as holding virtual-currency and money-transmitter licenses; Circle separately has a NY limited-purpose trust company.

Circle reports USDC circulation of $70.0B and reserves of $71.4B on 2026-10-29. Its public reserve categories include bank deposits, overnight reverse Treasury repo and short-dated U.S. Treasuries; it reports weekly reserve disclosures and monthly Big Four assurance.

Standard Custody & Trust Company LLC is the current RLUSD issuer and a NYDFS limited-purpose trust company. The accessible August 2026 attestation reports 2.326B outstanding units and $2.446B reserves at August 31.
The August RLUSD reserve report lists Treasury bills ($1.557B), government money-market funds ($467.6M) and cash deposits ($421.6M).
Ripple reports RLUSD circulation of $2.627B and reserve funds of $2.7586B on October 29, but the accessible signed report found in this run covers August, not October.
Ripple National Trust Bank received final OCC approval on October 26 for reserve-management, collateral-trustee and fiduciary-custody activities. Standard Custody remains the RLUSD issuer.
BNY supports XRP and RLUSD custody and is RLUSD's primary reserve custodian. Direct mint/redeem through BNY and tokenized trade-finance initiatives are future plans.
Standard Chartered custody of RLUSD on XRPL is live; the Ripple/Standard Chartered/LMAX collateral-mirroring and eligibility work remains planned and subject to documentation, testing and approvals.
Bitnomial's current accepted-collateral page lists USD, BTC, ETH and XRP, not USDC or RLUSD.

competing_hypotheses.claim: USDC is the nearer-term payment-stablecoin collateral candidate because public issuer, reserve and assurance disclosures appear to align with the CFTC definition.
competing_hypotheses.counter: CFTC does not name USDC; no FCM notice or actual use found; DCO acceptance still matters for futures and cleared swaps.

competing_hypotheses.claim: RLUSD may qualify through Standard Custody's trust-company status.
competing_hypotheses.counter: Government-MMF look-through is not yet verified against the CFTC permitted-reserve list; current October balances lack an accessible October signed attestation.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Ripple's RNTB, BNY and Standard Chartered relationships could strengthen RLUSD institutional collateral utility.
competing_hypotheses.counter: RNTB is not the issuer; BNY mint/redeem and LMAX collateral integration remain planned.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Stablecoin collateral may support XRP derivatives indirectly without creating XRP spot demand.
competing_hypotheses.counter: Actual FCM usage, collateral balances, conversion flows and resulting XRP inventory changes are unknown.

capital_flow_rules: Customer stablecoin collateral is not automatically new capital; it can be existing inventory moved between accounts.
An FCM's own stablecoins deposited as residual interest are proprietary firm capital, not customer capital, and carry applicable capital charges.
Stablecoin circulation, reserve value, mint/burn, transfers and XRP spot purchases are separate series.
Stablecoin collateral does not imply XRP purchase unless a conversion or inventory change is independently evidenced.
